sessions.description: Every enterprise chasing AI value reaches for the same fix: a better model. That's the wrong diagnosis — the model was never the hard part. Traditional analytics already answered "what and why" questions; the enterprise goal today is a better decision, made faster and more consistently, at scale. But ask an enterprise what its AI initiative needs and the answer is almost always the same: a model, an agent, a data platform. That's what gets scoped, budgeted, and hired for — the hammer already in hand, looking for its nail. Enterprise-scale decision intelligence has a clear anatomy: signals → intelligence (predictions & forecasting) → simulation → recommendation → decision orchestration → execution (with human oversight) → audit. A decision-maker, an approver, and an executor move through that same chain differently - a different view, a different set of permissions, a different task. The value only shows up when this intelligence is built into the business process itself — not bolted on as a one-size-fits-all dashboard. That's the end-to-end decision product very few enterprises are building — the one that owns the full value chain: a role-aware decision experience, human-and-agent collaboration, embedded intelligence, process orchestration, enterprise integration, and governance, with oversight designed in, not bolted on after. As AI coding assistants rewrite build-vs-buy economics, engineering that full value chain — not just the model — becomes the enterprise's real differentiator.

In contrast, the industry's cutting edge is shifting toward 'AI-native' development. These systems are designed from inception with AI as a core structural component, rather than an add-on feature. By moving past cosmetic integrations, this session will analyze exactly who stands to benefit in the long run, how organizations can successfully navigate this deep adoption curve, and why building with AI as an organic foundation is the only way to secure a competitive advantage in the industry.

sessions.title: How to Govern AI even If It's Hard to Predict

speakers.name: Kunal Das
speakers.title: Developer Advocate
speakers.bio: Kunal Das is Developer Advocate (APAC) at Kimchi.dev , where he focuses on helping engineering teams adopt governed AI coding agents. sessions.description: Nobody truly understands AI. Not even the people building it. Models behave in ways no one can fully predict, improve along paths no one can map, and carry risks that regulation hasn't caught up with. But unpredictability doesn't make governance impossible. It means governance has to happen at the right layer. The default approach to governing AI is restriction: rate limits, model lock-in, single-vendor dependencies, manual sign-off on every step. It slows teams down without making anything safer or more accountable. Routing changes that. When an orchestrator classifies each task and sends it to the right model, a reasoning model for planning, a fast executor for bulk code, a strong reviewer for quality, governance happens through the routing itself rather than through a separate policy layer. Cost is controlled by how the system routes work. No single model is a single point of failure. Data stays where you want it. Humans set the rules that drive routing decisions, and the system handles the rest. This session walks through Kimchi's multi-model orchestration architecture to show how that works in practice. Five roles, automatic model selection, no vendor lock-in. You don't need to predict what AI will do. You need to control how decisions about AI get made. Routing gives you that control.

sessions.description: Most enterprise AI rests on software-industry assumptions — experimentation is cheap, payback can be slow, adoption can be mandated. Businesses operating on single-digit margins have none of that latitude, and that constraint imposes a discipline the wider industry will need the moment AI budgets face the same scrutiny as every other line item. This session argues that building for customers who cannot absorb a failure produces better engineering: ruthless problem selection, payback measured in weeks, and success defined by outcomes rather than activity. It closes with a prediction about which programmes survive the returns question when it arrives.

This talk will focus on our journey of building an enterprise ready AI at scale, challenges encountered and the lessons learned.

sessions.title: Right for the Wrong Reasons: An Honest Audit of AI in 2026

sessions.description: A year ago, I warned that context windows couldn't scale, models couldn't decompose genuinely hard problems, and the enterprise returns would disappoint. The scorecard is in, and the skeptics won: "context rot" is now a benchmarked fact, and Gartner projects 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by 2027. Of the thousands of vendors selling "agents," fewer than 2% are selling the real thing. Are we heading towards an LLM dead-end? Here is the uncomfortable part: being right changed absolutely nothing. Investment accelerated, and so did actual capability. The strangest findings of the year are going completely undiscussed. Developers using AI measurably ship slower while feeling 20% faster, yet 90% of employees quietly extract real value from AI tools their companies never officially approved. The technology was never the bottleneck. History is repeating itself: most firms are using a revolutionary technology to stubbornly preserve the exact operating models it was meant to replace. Closing the gap between what AI actually does and what we believe it does is the hardest problem in tech today—and inside a regulated financial firm, you have to do it with zero room for error. Impossible just takes longer. Join me for a CTO's audit of what’s real, what’s pure theatre, and where the real capabilities are still locked.

sessions.description: Do Machine Learning models still matter in the Era of Agentic AI? Business Decisions by AI Agents: Real, or a Myth? Yes! For reliable decision intelligence, traditional machine learning still reigns supreme. Classical ML models are mathematically grounded, explainable, and optimized for high performance in structured environments, something Agentic AI alone cannot guarantee. Agentic AI can orchestrate and enhance its use, unlocking new possibilities for integrated intelligence. Think of Agentic AI as the conductor, while traditional ML models are expert musicians, each skilled in a particular instrument.

Bring together an IndiaAI Mission representative, a sovereign foundation model founder (Sarvam, Krutrim), a hyperscaler India head, and a policy voice from Carnegie or Ananta Aspen.

Beyond the Capital Gap: Why India Holds the Future for Building Sovereign Deep-Tech Hardware

speakers.title: Founder & Technical Lead

Yet these sectors require patient capital, specialised talent, infrastructure and long development cycles. This session will explore how India can bridge these gaps by connecting academia, industry, government and investors to commercialise frontier research, build critical IP and create globally competitive deep-tech companies. It will examine whether India can move from being a technology consumer and integrator to becoming a global builder of sovereign deep-tech hardware.

sessions.title: Own the Margin: Owning our AI to serve the customers everyone else's models miss

speakers.name: Debarya Dutta
speakers.title: Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO)
speakers.bio: Debarya Dutta is the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO) at True Balance, where he leads the company's AI-first transformation across products, operations, risk management, and customer experience. As the head of the newly established AI division, he is responsible for integrating artificial intelligence into the core of the organization's decision-making processes, helping build scalable financial solutions for the next generation of underserved and emerging consumers. A technology and AI leader with experience spanning global technology and financial ecosystems, Debarya brings expertise in machine learning, AI strategy, data science, and large-scale intelligent systems. Prior to joining True Balance, he held AI leadership roles at Uber and has worked extensively at the intersection of artificial intelligence, analytics, product innovation, and business transformation. He is an alumnus of the University of Cambridge and the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), institutions recognized globally for excellence in mathematics, statistics, and artificial intelligence. At True Balance, Debarya is driving the company's vision of becoming an AI-native financial platform, leveraging AI to enhance credit assessment, personalization, fraud detection, customer engagement, and operational efficiency. His work focuses on creating intelligent financial infrastructure that expands access to formal financial services for millions of underserved users across India and other emerging markets.

sessions.description: The borrowers hardest to judge, thin-file, first-time, informal-economy are the ones the credit system sees least clearly, and the ones True Balance exists to serve. The industry models don't fail these customers by disagreeing about them; they fail them together. Built on the same general-purpose foundations and reading the same sparse bureau signals, everyone is blind in the same place, for the same reason. The standard response is to layer more features onto that shared base. Ours is to change the substrate: learn representations from first-party data no one else has, rather than inherit them from foundations everyone shares, and make those representations the single backbone under every lending decision. Our data is a genuine moat: 200 billion+ financial transactions across 100 million+ users, spanning years. But scale, in principle, is copyable. What isn't is the legitimacy to use consented, first-party behavioral data assembled under India's DPDP and RBI digital-lending regimes. The moat is the data and the right to learn from it. This talk is about teaching a machine to read a financial life. We treat a user's transaction stream not as a table of features but as a sequence unfolding in time and we model the numbers themselves: the amounts, the balances, the EMIs, the gaps between events, not merely that an event occurred. Trained only to predict what comes next, the model has to learn the shape of how money moves through a life when it arrives, how long it lasts, what gets paid first when it runs short. That shape is the credit signal. And it is precisely the part of a person the bureau, built to read formal records, was never able to see. The honest difficulty is that this signal is most valuable exactly where it is hardest to check. A representation whose whole purpose is to speak for the people with the thinnest records is one you cannot validate the easy way against clean labels that, for these customers, mostly don't exist. How you build conviction in it anyway is the real content of this talk. What comes out is a single dense representation of a person's financial fingerprint that sharpens credit risk, fraud, and the next action we offer each customer, and tomorrow becomes the substrate for something larger: instead of judging people based on records they don't have, we understand them based on their actual life.

sessions.title: From Data to Decisions to Action: The Next Frontier of AI in Agriculture

speakers.name: Ravishankar Cherukuri
speakers.title: CEO
speakers.bio: Ravishankar Cherukuri is currently CEO, UPL Sustainable Agriculture Solutions (SAS). He has leadership experience at Bayer, where he led digital and GTM transformation in India and Asia, and at Monsanto, where he was MD & CEO. Before Agriculture, Ravi has worked across sectors and functions in organizations like BCG and Unilever. Ravi holds an MBA from the Indian School of Business and a bachelor’s degree in chemical engineering from IIT Kharagpur

sessions.description: Agriculture is entering a new era where AI is moving beyond data collection and prediction to enabling faster, smarter, and more actionable decisions. From satellite imagery and weather data to soil intelligence, crop monitoring, and farm-level insights, the opportunity lies in connecting diverse data sources and translating them into meaningful actions for farmers and agricultural stakeholders. This session will explore how AI can bridge the gap between data, decisions, and action across the agricultural value chain. It will examine the role of AI in predicting crop health and yields, optimizing inputs, identifying risks, improving resource efficiency, and enabling more personalized interventions. The discussion will also look at the challenges of taking AI solutions from pilots to real-world adoption, including data quality, accessibility, trust, scalability, and the need to build solutions suited to India's diverse farming ecosystems. Ultimately, the session will highlight how the next frontier of AI in agriculture is not simply about generating better insights, but about turning those insights into timely, scalable, and measurable action helping build a more productive, resilient, and technology-driven agricultural ecosystem in India.

speakers.title: VP- Business Growth & Delivery
speakers.bio: Business Growth and Delivery at KPI Partners, with over 16 years of experience across consulting, delivery, and growth. Sumar's focus is bridging the gap between experimentation and real-world impact, combining strong data engineering foundations with scalable AI architectures.

sessions.description: Enterprise AI has a pattern nobody likes to say out loud. The demos impress, the pilots get funded, and most never reach production or move the P&L. The teams that break through are not the ones with better models. Everyone has the same models. They own the layer underneath. India's Global Capability Centers are shifting from running AI built elsewhere to building it themselves. But capability is downstream of context, and most centers skip the data and context layer that decides whether AI actually works. That is exactly where pilots stall. This session unpacks the recurring failure patterns behind stalled AI programs and the operating model that separates the builders from the rest: modernize the foundation, engineer context, evaluate rigorously, operationalize. You will leave with a clear view of what production-grade looks like, plus accelerators and real outcomes from deployments. Making AI in India means building a layer that no one can rent.

sessions.title: Explainability is an infrastructure problem, not a model problem

speakers.name: Tushar Haldar
speakers.title: Founder and CEO
speakers.bio: Tushar Haldar is the Founder and CEO of ARA AI Labs (Pune). A distributed systems engineer and IEEE Senior Member with nearly two decades building large-scale data platforms in India and Silicon Valley (ex Unity, Oracle), he holds a granted US patent in large-scale data systems. A career spent on infrastructure where scale, performance, and correctness leave no room for shortcuts shapes how he sees AI: as software moves from predictions to decisions, the systems beneath matter as much as the models on top. He returned to India in 2025 to build around the question he expects will define the coming decade: what it takes for autonomous software to remember, and account for, what it does. ARA launched in July 2026 with published, reproducible benchmarks (13.8M feature values/s sustained, 2.8s failover with zero acknowledged loss), and its core architecture is the subject of a pending US patent application.

sessions.description: An ML system declines a credit application at 14:32 on a Tuesday. Six weeks later a regulator, the customer, or your own risk team asks why. In most production stacks nobody can answer, because the feature values were overwritten by the next update, the model was retrained twice, and the world the model saw at that instant is gone. SHAP, LIME, and model cards describe how a model behaves in general; accountability is about one decision in particular, and that record was never kept. The thesis of the talk: you cannot explain a decision whose inputs you never recorded. Explainability is a data architecture gap, not a modelling gap.

sessions.title: Research, Capability, Sovereignty: Building Frontier AI from India

speakers.name: Parth Sarthi
speakers.title: Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Parth Sarthi is the Co-Founder of Chariot, a frontier AI research lab headquartered in Delhi and one of original four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build the country's foundation models. Prior to co-founding Chariot, Parth was a Research Engineer at Google DeepMind, where he worked on multimodal reasoning for Gemini DeepThink and on long-context research. Before that he was the fourth research hire at Contextual AI, founded by Douwe Kiela, the inventor of retrieval-augmented generation, where he worked on retrieval models and training infrastructure. At Stanford, as a sophomore, he created RAPTOR, a recursive tree-structured retrieval technique that set a new state of the art and pioneered hierarchical generative retrieval. Published at ICLR 2024 and cited more than 900 times, RAPTOR has become a standard method for RAG and is built into LangChain and LlamaIndex. He was also co-first author on Optimas, a framework for optimizing multi-agent AI systems. Parth studied Computer Science at Stanford University, working with the Stanford NLP Group and the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (SAIL), advised by Christopher Manning and Anna Goldie. He was a member of the Stanford team that won the $250,000 Science Innovation Prize at the Alexa Prize. In 2020, he was awarded the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar by the Prime Minister, India's highest civilian honour for citizens under 18, for reuniting missing children with their families. His areas of expertise include speech AI, large language models and retrieval-augmented generation.

speakers.name: Suvrat Bhooshan
speakers.title: Co-Founder

sessions.description: Chariot is one of the first four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign foundation models. speakers.name: Kakul Paul
speakers.title: Partner & Delivery Unit Leader
speakers.bio: Kakul Paul is a Partner and Delivery Unit Leader at Tiger Analytics, with over two decades of experience shaping enterprise transformation through AI, advanced analytics and data-led strategy. She works with organizations to unlock the value of data, build high-performing Analytics Centers of Excellence and scale multidisciplinary teams from strategy to execution. Kakul brings a distinctive blend of business, technology and entrepreneurial experience, having begun her career in CPG marketing at GSK Consumer Healthcare before moving into analytics consulting and leadership roles at Accenture and Brillio. She was also part of the founding teams of analytics ventures Marketics and Marketelligent. Her industry experience spans CPG, retail, hospitality, gaming, logistics and utilities. An IIT (BHU) Varanasi and IIM Ahmedabad alumna, Kakul brings a pragmatic, business-focused perspective to enterprise AI adoption and transformation.

speakers.name: Vaishnavi Kandala
speakers.title: Head of AI Labs
speakers.bio: Vaishnavi heads AI Labs at Tiger Analytics, where she leads the company’s efforts to shape what comes next in enterprise AI. Her work spans applied R&D and collaborations with clients, leading AI labs, hyperscalers, and academia. She also leads Tiger’s thinking on AI-native enterprise operating models, including how technology and business value chains can be reimagined with AI. She focuses on translating frontier innovation into practical enterprise adoption and has led multiple large-scale implementations of AI solutions across global enterprises.

sessions.description: While foundational models provide a powerful reasoning engine, they lack the unique operational DNA of your business required for meaningful action. The Context Layer acts as the critical bridge, securely injecting your real-time data, permissions, and domain logic into a well connected ontology that feeds the autonomous workflows. Join this session to discover how grounding AI in your enterprise truth is the ultimate secret sauce for moving agentic applications out of the lab and into production.

sessions.title: The Last-Mile AI Problem: Building Technology for Users Outside the Digital Mainstream

speakers.name: Madhav Krishna
speakers.title: Founder and CEO
speakers.bio: Madhav Krishna is the Founder & CEO of Vahan.ai , an AI-powered recruitment platform transforming hiring for India's 500+ million blue-collar workforce. Since founding the company in 2016, he has led its mission to make employment more accessible by leveraging AI and automation to connect millions of job seekers with opportunities across industries. With a background in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Madhav is passionate about applying technology to solve large-scale workforce challenges. Under his leadership, Vahan.ai has emerged as one of India's leading AI-driven hiring platforms, backed by investors including Y Combinator, Khosla Ventures, and Bharti Airtel. Recognized as a Technology Pioneer by the World Economic Forum, Madhav is committed to shaping the future of work by building intelligent, scalable solutions that empower both employers and job seekers. His work sits at the intersection of AI, employment, and digital inclusion, driving meaningful impact across India's workforce.

sessions.description: AI has made remarkable advances, but much of today’s technology is still designed around digitally fluent users who can read, type, navigate apps, and communicate in standardized languages. This creates a significant last-mile gap for millions of people outside the digital mainstream. This session explores what it takes to build AI for the next billion users, where voice, language, accessibility, connectivity, trust, and local context are not peripheral considerations but fundamental to the user experience. Drawing from the challenges of building voice-first and multilingual AI for India’s blue-collar workforce, the session will examine why voice can become a powerful interface for inclusive AI and why simply translating a model is not enough to truly understand how people communicate. It will explore how AI systems can be designed around real-world behaviour, diverse languages and accents, code-switching, low-connectivity environments, and highly contextual interactions—ultimately asking whether we are building AI for those who already know how to use technology, or for those who have been left out of the digital mainstream.

sessions.title: Build with Bob: It's More Than Just a Vibe

speakers.name: HS Manoj Kumar
speakers.title: Software Developer
speakers.bio: Manoj Kumar H S is a Software Engineer at IBM specializing in Generative AI, AI agents, RAG systems, and developer productivity. He works on building production AI solutions at IBM and has been actively involved in technology conferences, client engagements, developer events, and global AI initiatives. Manoj also coordinates Bobathons across 20+ global locations, engaging developers and enterprise teams in AI-powered software development. He has a research background in Machine Learning and NLP, with three peer-reviewed publications, and has received multiple awards for his work in AI and software innovation.

speakers.name: Aanchal Narendran
speakers.title: Software Developer
speakers.bio: Aanchal Narendran is a Software Developer at IBM's AI Centre of Excellence, where she designs and ships production-grade agentic AI systems. A tech lead across multiple projects, she builds both the agents and the platforms behind them: Agent Skills, RAG and ingestion pipelines, MCP tooling, and evaluation frameworks. She began her career in data and analytics at JPMorgan Chase, which shapes how she designs AI around real business decisions. Aanchal has published research in machine learning and deep learning and writes regularly for Open Source For You on AI and data topics, from production ML monitoring to in-process analytics. She has been recognised with multiple IBM awards for technical leadership and AI innovation, and shares her work through talks and developer workshops.

sessions.description: Experience IBM Bob through a guided, hands-on lab designed for developers. Build AI-powered applications, generate and modernize code, integrate APIs, debug faster, and explore real-world enterprise development workflows. Leave with practical skills, working examples, and the confidence to start building with IBM Bob in your own projects. Hands-on Lab Requirement:Participants are requested to bring their own laptop for the best experience.

sessions.title: Stop counting tokens. Start measuring outcomes.

speakers.name: Ritesh Dhoot
speakers.title: Executive Vice President - Engineering
speakers.bio: Ritesh Dhoot is a seasoned engineering leader with over two decades of experience building technology organizations. As the former Founder of Agricx Ritesh pioneered world-first AI and deep-learning platforms for agricultural quality assessment, with patents filed in image processing and computer vision. His entrepreneurial background is complemented by a distinguished career scaling global engineering hubs for Cisco, H1.co , Orange Health Labs, and BYJU’S. A specialist in distributed systems, Generative AI, and big data, Ritesh excels at aligning product, platform, and people to accelerate growth. Beyond his technical and operational expertise, he is an active angel investor and advisor, dedicated to driving the next generation of sovereign AI infrastructure. Outside of engineering, Ritesh is a cinematic enthusiast who approaches film through an architectural lens and finds creative balance playing the keyboard.

sessions.description: AI agents are moving beyond conversations to completing real-world tasks—but the cost of those outcomes is rarely captured by the token price alone. Follow one AI-powered insurance renewal call to uncover the real bill behind inference, including repeated context, caching, idle capacity, data movement, tooling and operational overhead. Then explore how to measure cost per successful outcome , and the architectural choices that can bring that number under control.

sessions.title: How ShareChat built an AI-powered understanding of regional cultures capturing the digital attention of Bharat

speakers.name: Nitin Jain
speakers.title: Chief Technology Officer
speakers.bio: Nitin Jain is the Chief Technology Officer at ShareChat, where he leads the company's technology vision, strategy, and execution to drive innovation at scale. With over two decades of experience across e-commerce, fintech, digital advertising, and AI-driven platforms, he has built and scaled high-performance engineering organizations that power some of Asia's fastest-growing internet businesses. Before joining ShareChat, Nitin served as Head of Ecommerce Ads Tech at TikTok Indonesia and held multiple senior leadership roles at Tokopedia, including Senior Vice President of Engineering. At Tokopedia, he led technology across Ad Solutions, FinTech, Payments, AI-powered Search & Personalization, and spearheaded the launch of the company's crypto trading business from the ground up. His work has been instrumental in developing large-scale, AI-powered platforms that deliver personalized customer experiences, advanced advertising capabilities, digital payments, lending, and financial services. Nitin's expertise spans artificial intelligence, machine learning, programmatic advertising, fintech, blockchain, cloud computing, recommender systems, and large-scale distributed systems. Throughout his career, he has played a pivotal role in the rapid growth of several high-growth startups and unicorns by building world-class engineering teams and delivering technology platforms that drive business transformation and customer impact.

sessions.description: As AI reshapes the digital ecosystem, the next frontier lies in understanding culture – not just language. This session will explore how ShareChat has built AI-powered systems that decode regional preferences, cultural nuances and evolving consumer behaviour to deliver deeply personalised content experiences for Bharat. It will also examine the rise of microdramas as a high-engagement content format, and how AI is enabling the convergence of storytelling, content discovery and commerce, redefining how creators, audiences and brands connect in India's multilingual digital ecosystem.

sessions.title: Building an AI-Native Non-Profit: Reimagining Social Impact in the Age of AI

speakers.name: Navya Naveli Nanda
speakers.title: Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Navya Naveli Nanda is a social entrepreneur working at the intersection of gender equity, technology and inclusive growth. As Founder of Project Naveli, she leads initiatives that expand access to markets, capital and knowledge networks for women entrepreneurs across emerging towns in India. Through its flagship platform, Entreprenaari, the organisation is building long-term economic infrastructure that enables women-led enterprises to scale sustainably. As Co-Founder of Nimaya, Navya has led the effort to make over 10,000 young women across five states GenAI-ready - ensuring that women are not excluded from the structural shifts reshaping the future of work, but are equipped to participate meaningfully and competitively within it. She also works closely with the leadership of Escorts Kubota, contributing to efforts that democratise access to advanced agricultural technologies, innovation and data systems for India’s farming communities - strengthening productivity and resilience at the grassroots level. A UN Women Gender Ally and recipient of recognitions including GQ Influential Person of the Year and Entrepreneur’s Women Leader of the Year, Navya is currently pursuing her MBA at IIM Ahmedabad, deepening her focus on institution-building and scalable impact. She is also co-authoring The Map, to be published by HarperCollins India - a playbook designed to equip India’s Gen Z with the frameworks to think independently, exercise agency and navigate a world transformed by AI, social media and techno-capital systems

speakers.name: Samyak Chakrabarty
speakers.title: Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Samyak is the Founder and Chief Architect of Workverse, a virtual world of work where professionals enhance their workplace intelligence and master soft skills. With over 18 years of entrepreneurial experience, he is on a mission to empower humans to outsmart artificial intelligence at work. He has been featured by Forbes as one of Asia's most influential young entrepreneurs and has founded several social impact initiatives, such as The Green Batti Project, India's largest one-on-one mentoring program for youth, and Operation Black Dot, a campaign to increase voter awareness and participation among college students. He also has a passion for youth diplomacy and peace-building, having organized and chaired the first-ever Indo-Pak Youth Peace Summit and built the country's largest M.U.N Platform - Indian International Model United Nations. He has also been appointed by the U.N in India to be president over their annual Young Changemakers Conclave.

sessions.description: As AI reshapes the way organisations work, the social sector has an opportunity to rethink not just the tools it uses, but how it is built from the ground up. This session will explore what it means to become an AI-native non-profit—moving beyond isolated AI use cases to embedding AI into everyday operations, decision-making, programme delivery, and organisational strategy. Using Nimaya's journey as a real-world case study, Navya and Samyak will share practical lessons, successes, and challenges in building an organisation where AI enhances efficiency, increases transparency, and enables teams to spend more time on innovation and impact. Attendees will leave with a new perspective on how mission-driven organisations can leverage AI to build smarter, more scalable, and future-ready institutions.

sessions.title: The One Place AI Can’t Pretend — And Why Every Industry Is Next

speakers.name: Jagadeesh Ramasamy
speakers.title: CIO & CDO
speakers.bio: Jagadeesh Ramasamy is the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and Chief Information Officer (CIO) at Narayana Health , where he leads the organization's digital transformation, technology strategy, and innovation initiatives. With over two decades of experience in healthcare technology, product development, and enterprise IT, he has played a pivotal role in building scalable digital platforms that enhance patient care and operational excellence. Prior to his current role, he served as Head of Product at athmâ and previously spent seven years leading clinical and business applications at Narayana Health across India and the Cayman Islands. Jagadeesh is passionate about leveraging AI, digital platforms, and emerging technologies to shape the future of healthcare.

sessions.description: AI is moving from experimentation to real-world impact, but healthcare is one of the places where its promises must stand up to reality. In this session, Jagadeesh Ramasamy explores why healthcare can be a powerful proving ground for AI—where accuracy, trust, human outcomes, and accountability cannot be simulated. The discussion will examine how lessons from healthcare are relevant across industries as organizations move from AI pilots to scaled, responsible adoption. From transforming patient experiences and operational decision-making to building trust in intelligent systems, the session will explore what it takes to turn AI from a technology narrative into measurable, industry-wide impact.

Before Best Buy, he helped keep Amazon's marketplace safe and trustworthy for millions of shoppers, and he led data science at American Express and ZEE5. Vishal is passionate about building AI that is practical and responsible, and about growing the teams who build it.

sessions.description: Design a task-oriented AI agent that retrieves information, calls business tools, maintains workflow state and returns structured outputs. Participants learn the engineering foundations required to move beyond prompting toward dependable enterprise agents.

sessions.title: Agent Harness for Enterprise: Engineering the Runtime for Reliable AI Agents

speakers.name: Manoranjan Rajguru
speakers.title: Applied AI, GTM
speakers.bio: Manoranjan Rajguru is an AI Architect at Microsoft, specializing in Generative AI and Large Language Models. With over a decade of experience in AI and ML, he previously served as a Data Scientist at Amazon. Manoranjan is a prominent figure in the tech community, contributing over 30 articles to Medium and maintaining a LinkedIn following of 8,000 professionals. His expertise and thought leadership have significantly influenced technical advancements and shaped the AI landscape. Manoranjan's work continues to drive innovation and impact in the field of artificial intelligence.

sessions.description: Enterprise AI agents are evolving from simple tool-calling assistants into autonomous systems capable of reasoning, planning, executing workflows, and collaborating with other agents. However, deploying these agents in production requires more than a powerful model and a collection of tools. An Agent Harness provides the engineering and runtime layer that governs how agents discover skills, manage context, select and execute tools, delegate tasks, recover from failures, verify results, and operate within enterprise security and compliance boundaries. In this session, we will explore the architecture of an enterprise-grade Agent Harness, covering progressive skill discovery, context compaction, multi-agent delegation, execution control, verification loops, identity propagation, observability, and governance. We will connect these patterns to real-world enterprise scenarios using Azure AI Foundry and modern agentic AI frameworks. The session will provide a practical blueprint for building AI agents that are not just capable of completing tasks, but are *reliable, observable, governed, and ready for enterprise-scale adoption.

sessions.title: The Agentic Platform: Powering Operations for Real Business Outcomes

speakers.title: Chief Architect
speakers.bio: Rakesh Shinde is a Chief Architect at Genpact with over three decades of experience in the IT industry. A Master Inventor with more than eight patents to his name, he champions innovative and emerging technologies to solve real business challenges. He currently leads the development of responsible agentic AI solutions at Genpact, helping clients improve efficiency across their corporate functions.

sessions.description: Agentic AI is moving from experimentation to real business operations. This session explores how to build a shared platform for responsible, scalable agentic solutions—bringing together orchestration, context, enterprise integration and governance to deliver measurable business outcomes.

sessions.title: AI filmmaking

speakers.name: Vatsal Sheth
speakers.title: Co founder - CEO
speakers.bio: Vatsal Sheth is the Co-Founder & CEO of Prismix Studios, an AI-first creative studio at the forefront of blending generative AI with filmmaking, visual effects, advertising, and digital content production. Under his leadership, Prismix Studios is redefining how stories are created by combining cutting-edge AI technologies with human creativity to deliver high-quality, scalable, and visually compelling content. The studio has been recognized for pioneering AI-powered storytelling through projects such as Happy Birthday Joshi and other innovative cinematic productions. A well-known actor and entrepreneur, Vatsal has successfully bridged the worlds of entertainment and technology. Drawing on his extensive experience in the media industry, he is championing the use of AI to democratize storytelling, enabling creators and brands to bring ambitious ideas to life with greater speed, efficiency, and creative freedom. His vision is helping shape the future of AI-driven content creation in India and beyond

sessions.description: AI is reshaping filmmaking from how stories are imagined and scripted to how scenes are visualised, produced, edited, and brought to life. This session will explore the emerging world of AI filmmaking and how creators can use generative AI to expand creative possibilities while rethinking traditional production workflows. Vatsal Sheth will share insights into the intersection of technology and storytelling, exploring what AI means for filmmakers, the evolving role of the creator, and the future of cinema in an AI-first era.

sessions.title: Who Controls the Stack Controls the State: Mogging global-AI in a hostile world.

speakers.name: Anuraag Saxena
speakers.title: Market Access & Public Policy Leader
speakers.bio: Anuraag Saxena advises late-stage startups, companies and navigating complex regulatory environments, public policy, geo-politics, and building narratives. He is a nominated member of Government of India National Councils, founder of India Pride Project, and a published public policy expert. His work has been featured on BBC, Washington Post, Doordarshan, Times of India, Economic Times, Sunday Guardian, The Diplomat, Man’s World, Span, Organiser, and Panchajanya; and has spoken at Universities and Conferences across the world. Anuraag has worked and written extensively about Public Policy, Corporate Affairs, GeoPolitics, and Regulatory Affairs He also co-founded India Pride Project (the world’s first crowd- sourced heritage-recovery project). Before that, he spent his corporate years with GE Capital, Deutsche Bank and Credit Suisse.

sessions.description: AI companies are not just navigating domestic regulations, but a minefield of international geopolitical battles. In an era of digital sovereignty, security concerns, tariff wars, and visa ambiguity; managing global growth and competition, needs an elevated set of skills and access, beyond technology. In this talk, we discuss the hostility frontier technology operators face from across the borders, and strategies for navigating the new world order of frontier technologies.

sessions.title: AI can build almost anything. What should we build?

speakers.name: Jennifer Mecherippady
speakers.title: Senior Vice-President and AI Leader, Asia Pacific Global Delivery Centers of Excellence
speakers.bio: Jennifer Mecherippady leads CGI's Insurance & Health Business Unit within the Asia Pacific Global Delivery Centers of Excellence, driving strategy, growth and technology-enabled transformation for clients across the insurance, healthcare and life sciences sectors. With more than 30 years of experience, Jennifer has led large-scale business transformation, innovation and global delivery organizations. She also leads CGI's AI transformation agenda across APAC, working with CGI’s global technology teams, hyperscalers and alliance partners to accelerate enterprise adoption of AI and generative AI and develop industry-focused solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes. Previously, Jennifer led CGI's intellectual property organization in APAC, helping modernize and scale strategic platforms and solutions across banking, insurance, utilities, healthcare and government. A passionate mentor and people leader, Jennifer champions talent development, mentorship and inclusion initiatives across CGI’s APAC operations, helping develop the next generation of technology and business leaders.

sessions.description: AI has made execution abundant. Judgment is now the differentiator. As the cost of building falls, enterprises face a new and potentially more expensive risk: building more, faster without creating more value. The defining question is no longer simply What can AI create? It is Where should we focus our data, investment and attention? In this keynote, Jennifer Mecherippady explores the new economics of enterprise AI and why better judgment, not simply greater technical capability, will determine which investments create value at scale. Drawing on CGI’s experience and conversations with clients, she will break down how proprietary data creates real advantage, how context and enterprise knowledge can make AI more useful, how model dependency can lead to hidden costs and limit flexibility, and how token economics are changing the cost equation. The opportunity is not simply to build more with AI. It is to apply the judgment needed to build what matters.

sessions.title: Transforming Enterprise development with the new AI-SDLC

speakers.name: Madhuri D. Madhavanpillai
speakers.title: Program Director, Engineering Leader, AI-Powered Business Analytics, IBM India Software Labs, Kochi
speakers.bio: Madhuri D. Madhavanpillai is a Program Director and Senior Engineering Leader at IBM Software, leading an AI-powered Business Analytics portfolio. With 24 years of experience in technology and engineering leadership, she has led software design, development, support, technical program and client management across Systems Management, Virtualization, Cloud Security, Data and AI. A technologist and innovator, Madhuri is a patent holder and published author, with a strong passion for transforming technology into business and societal impact. She actively contributes to the industry–academia ecosystem and serves on the Board of Studies at Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT) and several other engineering institutions. Madhuri is an IEEE Senior Member and an active industry leader with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). She serves as Convenor of the AI Adoption and Digital Transformation pillar of CII Kerala and is a member of the CII Southern Region Taskforce on AI Adoption & Responsible Deployment and the CII Southern Region Taskforce on Higher Education Excellence & Industry–Academia Nexus. Her interests span AI, engineering transformation, responsible AI adoption, innovation, and building strong bridges between industry and academia.

sessions.description: AI is redefining how modern software is built. From planning and coding to testing, deployment, and operations, AI is accelerating every stage of the Software Development Lifecycle. Join this keynote to explore how developers are embracing AI-native workflows, boosting productivity, and delivering software faster—setting the stage for the next evolution of developer experiences with IBM Bob

sessions.title: From Insight to Action: The Power of AI Operations

speakers.name: Richa Vivek Savant
speakers.title: Engineer I
speakers.bio: Richa Vivek Savant graduated from Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham with a degree in Computer Science and Engineering in 2025. She joined StoneX Group Inc. after graduation and currently works as an Application Engineer, where she bridges the gap between end-user requirements and technical solutions by building automation-driven solutions and improving operational workflows and reliability. Her professional interests include software engineering, intelligent automation, and agentic AI. She is particularly interested in using emerging technologies to improve how enterprise applications are designed, automated, and integrated to solve practical operational challenges.

sessions.description: From Insight to Action: The Power of AI Operations explores how proactive AI can transform enterprise operations from reactive incident management to intelligent, always-on response. The session shows how AI can bring together signals across complex technology environments to detect issues earlier, accelerate investigation and resolution, and reduce dependency on scarce SME expertise. At its core, it demonstrates how combining human judgment with proactive AI can create more resilient operations, keep customers better informed, and ultimately strengthen customer trust.

sessions.title: How AI is disrupting the Legal Services sector

speakers.name: Kapil Chaudhary
speakers.title: Co-Founder & Joint Managing Partner
speakers.bio: Kapil Chaudhary is Co-Founder and Joint Managing Partner of Verity Law Chambers, an independent chambers advising boards, general counsel, and founders on AI governance, data privacy, technology and platform regulation, and technology-driven disputes. He brings 26 years of experience across senior in-house leadership and private practice, with a practical, operator-led perspective on the legal and regulatory challenges facing global technology companies, digital platforms, and data-driven businesses. Prior to founding Verity Law Chambers, Kapil was a Partner in the Technology, Media & Telecommunications and Data Privacy practice at Dentons Link Legal. Before that, he served as General Counsel and in senior legal leadership roles at IBM, Autodesk, Twitter, Flutter International / Junglee Games, Schlumberger, and Info Edge (India) Limited — advising boards and leadership teams through periods of rapid innovation, heightened regulatory scrutiny, and market expansion. His software licensing and technology-contracting practice draws directly on his tenure as India General Counsel at Autodesk, where he structured enterprise licensing, channel, and subscription programmes across South Asia. His media and entertainment practice spans an early role as Assistant Vice President – Legal at Star News Media, through to gaming, platform, and content regulation work at Twitter and Junglee Games (Flutter International). Clients value his ability to distil legal and regulatory risk into clear, decision-oriented advice for boards and senior management, aligned with commercial and strategic objectives. A significant part of his work involves advising boards, CEOs, and general counsel on the responsible deployment of AI and data at scale, particularly in regulated or reputation-sensitive sectors such as consumer internet, financial services, media, gaming, and global capability centres (GCCs).

sessions.description: Artificial intelligence is rewriting the legal profession from the inside out — transforming contract drafting, legal research, compliance, and regulatory decision-making, and forcing a redefinition of what legal professionals actually do. This session examines that disruption head-on: what's changing, how fast, and what it means for lawyers, GCs, and the institutions they serve. Drawing on more than two decades leading legal and policy functions inside global technology companies, Kapil will unpack the regulatory terrain now forming around AI — data privacy, intellectual property, platform governance, and responsible AI adoption — and make the case for a fundamental shift in how legal leaders operate. The argument: legal functions must move from risk containment to strategic enablement, building the trust, accountability, and compliance infrastructure that lets organisations actually harness AI rather than merely survive it.

sessions.title: From Trading Platform to Intelligence Platform: How AI is Redefining Investing in India

speakers.name: Ambarish Kenghe
speakers.title: Group Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Ambarish Kenghe is the Group Chief Executive Officer of Angel One Limited. With a dynamic career spanning FinTech, e-commerce, and consumer technology, Ambarish brings deep expertise in digital transformation, product innovation, and business scaling. Before Google, Ambarish served as Chief Product Officer at Myntra, where he spearheaded AI/ML-powered innovations, transforming the fashion e-commerce experience. His professional journey also includes strategy consulting at Bain & Company in San Francisco and engineering high-speed switching technologies at Cisco Systems in San Jose. A recognized innovator, Ambarish holds four patents and has a strong academic foundation, with a MBA from UC Berkeley, a Master’s degree in Computer Science from Purdue University, a Master’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering from IIT Kanpur and a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering from AMU. As Group CEO, Ambarish will focus on accelerating Angel One’s growth trajectory, driving product and technology innovation and enhancing customer experiences in the evolving FinTech ecosystem.

sessions.description: India’s investing landscape is undergoing a profound transformation. As millions of new investors enter the markets, the next wave of innovation is no longer just about enabling transactions—it is about delivering intelligence at scale. Artificial Intelligence is reshaping how investors discover opportunities, assess risks, make decisions, and build long-term wealth. In this session, Ambarish Kenghe will explore how AI is driving the evolution of investment platforms from execution-focused trading tools to intelligent financial companions. Drawing on his experience leading large-scale consumer technology and fintech products, he will discuss how AI-powered personalization, predictive insights, conversational interfaces, and data-driven recommendations are transforming the investing experience for millions of Indians. The session will also examine the opportunities and responsibilities that come with building AI-first financial products, including trust, transparency, accessibility, and financial inclusion. Attendees will gain insights into how technology leaders are shaping the future of investing and what it will take to build the next generation of intelligent wealth platforms in India

As AI systems reason, use tools and execute multi-step workflows, token consumption and cost can grow significantly—making workflow governance, cost per outcome and workload placement increasingly important. sessions.title: From AI Experiments to Business Impact: Building an AI-First Data Science Organization

speakers.name: Raunak Gulshan
speakers.title: Senior Director, GCC Growth & Transformation
speakers.bio: Raunak is a seasoned client partner in the Data Analytics & Management Consulting industry for 16+ years working with top Fortune 100 customers. He joined Tredence as the first employee in North America and for the last 10+ years, he has been a part of the growth story, since Tredence's early startup days. He has contributed not only through delivery leadership but also across business development, capability building, mentoring, and shaping scalable team structures. He is currently leading Tredence’s Global Capability Center (GCC) Business Unit to help global enterprise clients modernize, scale, and transform their capability centers into high-value innovation hubs via hyperscaler co-innovation and outcome-based AI solutions across key enterprise hubs. Prior to Tredence, Raunak was a part of Mu Sigma during its rapid growth phase. He worked across multiple industry verticals in India and the US, delivering large-scale analytics and building operating models to drive tangible business outcomes.

sessions.description: Retailers have moved beyond asking, “What can we do with GenAI?” to a much harder question: “Where can AI create measurable business impact?” As AI moves from experimentation into the enterprise, success is increasingly less about building impressive POCs and more about identifying the right problems, demonstrating measurable ROI, driving adoption, and operationalizing solutions at scale. Key points which we will explore during the discussion : Prioritizing for impact: Moving from a long list of AI possibilities to a focused portfolio of high-value use cases. From POC to production: What separates interesting experiments from AI solutions that can be deployed and scaled across the enterprise. Measuring AI ROI: Connecting technical outcomes and model performance to tangible business KPIs. Driving adoption: Why workflow integration, trust and change management are as critical as the underlying AI

sessions.title: Power, Water, Natural Resources and the Infinite Horizon: Why the Future of AI Compute May Belong to the Oceans and Space

speakers.name: Michael Ferrari
speakers.title: Chief AI Officer
speakers.bio: Dr. Michael Ferrari is the Vice President of Research at Moby, and Senior Partner at AlphaGeo. His work emphasizes commercializing basic and applied research towards a variety of scientific, technical, and economic domains sitting at the deep tech, data, and industrial interface. Most of his work sits at the AI-energy-water-infrastructure nexus, and explores the confluence of three emerging global trends: natural resource geoeconomics, the AI- energy transition and technological evolution. He has built applied research teams at numerous early stage companies, as well as several large global corporations, including Syngenta, Point72 Asset Management, IBM, and Mars. Dr. Ferrari earned his PhD from Rutgers University focusing on computational fluid dynamics, applied nuclear science and environmental biophysics, where his research centered on better understanding the industrial/environmental interface and the earth/space/biosphere complex from both an information systems and an evolutionary perspective. His doctoral work in numerical modeling and applied mathematics was supported by the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies in Manhattan.

sessions.description: The exponential growth of AI is rapidly colliding with Earth’s most precious resources: energy and water. In this forward-looking session at Cypher 2026, we will unpack the critical enablers and physical bottlenecks of the AI revolution, exploring how power grid constraints and water scarcity are dictating the current trajectory of innovation. To overcome these terrestrial limits, the industry must look beyond our shores and skies. We will dive into the radical next frontier of infrastructure - moving massive compute off-land into the natural cooling depths of our oceans, and off-planet into the boundless expanse and solar abundance of space. Join me to discover how leveraging these extreme environments could solve AI's escalating resource crisis and fundamentally redefine the future of global compute.

sessions.title: Human-Centred AI at Scale: How Haleon is Building the Future Through People, Trust and Technology

speakers.name: Richard Moule
speakers.title: Chief Data and Analytics Officer
speakers.bio: Richard Moule is a senior data and analytics leader with more than 20 years of experience driving business transformation through data, digital and AI. As Chief Data & AI Officer at Haleon, he is focused on accelerating the organisation's Data & AI strategy to unlock growth, improve decision-making and deliver business value at scale. Prior to Haleon, Richard spent six years at Reckitt leading global transformation programmes that increased efficiency, reduced costs and supported sustainable growth. He is passionate about translating strategic ambition into practical outcomes and building data-driven cultures that enable organisations to thrive in a rapidly evolving digital world.

sessions.description: As AI reshapes the future of work, success will not be determined by technology alone. It will depend on how organisations build trust, develop skills and empower people to work confidently alongside AI. In this keynote, Richard Moule, the Chief Data & Analytics Officer, will share how Haleon is delivering human-centred AI transformation at global scale to unlock productivity, growth and agility. He will highlight how Data & AI is helping teams make better decisions and create greater impact across some of the world's most trusted consumer health brands, including Eno, Sensodyne, Panadol, Advil, Centrum, Voltaren and Parodontax. Drawing on experiences from Haleon's global Data & AI transformation and the growth of the India Capability Centre, the speakers will discuss how investing in workforce capability, adoption and culture is helping create an organisation where people and AI can thrive together. Attendees will gain insight into the challenges many organisations face moving from technology deployment to true adoption, and how Haleon is fostering a ‘Win as One’ culture that combines leadership, learning and innovation to accelerate impact.

sessions.title: Make in India, See from India: Building sovereign space-AI capability

speakers.name: Suyash Singh
speakers.title: Co-founder and CEO
speakers.bio: Suyash is an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology (Madras) with a Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering. While at IIT, he assembled Team Avishkar to participate in the 2019 SpaceX Hyperloop Competition and led a motley group of prodigal engineers to develop India’s first self-propelled hyperloop pod prototype, becoming the only Asian finalist among 2,500 global participants. His expertise spans Deep Learning and Aerospace Engineering, which he uses to lead GalaxEye toward the launch of Drishti, the world’s first and only satellite providing high-resolution SyncFused OptoSAR™️imagery. This will be a game changer in the Earth Observation industry, as synchronised optical and SAR data would provide the most accurate, data-rich imagery of the Earth, available anytime, anywhere, in any weather. Recognised by Entrepreneur India as 35 under 35 and Fortune 40 under 40, and a sought-after speaker at global platforms like TEDx, Suyash’s visionary approach has garnered national and international acclaim for GalaxEye.

sessions.description: The session makes the case that AI sovereignty isn't just about LLMs and GPUs, it's also about who owns the satellites and sensors watching your own geography. Positions India's growing space-tech sector (GalaxEye as a live example) as a pillar of AI sovereignty most people aren't counting.

sessions.title: The AI Inflection Point: From Experimentation to Enterprise Transformation

speakers.name: Ruchika Panesar
speakers.title: Country Head, India and the Chief Information Officer, Functions
speakers.bio: Ruchika Panesar is the Country Head, India and the Chief Information Officer, Functions at the NatWest Group, a leading UK Bank. She is a transformational, purpose driven leader with a career spanning across Banking, FinTech and Payments disciplines. Her expertise lies in enterprise transformation driven by Technology, building enterprise grade products and platforms. She has successfully harnessed emerging technologies / AI / Gen AI across business domains to drive innovation and transformation at scale. Prior to joining NatWest Group, she spent over two decades at American Express based in New York and India, leading product development, engineering, and technology strategy development to drive best in class customer and colleague experiences. Ruchika is also a member of the Executive Council of Nasscom - India’s apex technology and industry trade body. She is passionate about education and skill development as a path to empowerment and is an active advocate and sponsor for underrepresented minorities, people in STEM.

sessions.description: AI is moving beyond the era of pilots, proofs of concept and isolated productivity gains. And we are approaching an inflection point where the real opportunity and challenge is to embed AI into the fabric of the enterprise.

sessions.title: DocLab: Bringing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System from Prototype to Production

speakers.name: Ravi Maggon
speakers.title: Associate Director, Tech
speakers.bio: Ravi Maggon is an Associate Director, Tech, at D. E. Shaw India, where he works as a member of the Generative AI Technology team. Ravi holds a bachelor's degree in computer science and engineering from Thapar University, Patiala.

sessions.description: This session explores how developers at D. E. Shaw India built a firmwide platform for employees to ask questions about large document collections and receive trustworthy, cited responses. Attendees will learn how the platform was built as shared infrastructure, rather than as a series of one-off experiments. They’ll also discover how our developers measure retrieval and answer quality and keep those measures reliable at scale. Useful for anyone taking a document-intelligence or RAG system from prototype to production for large-scale and varied datasets

sessions.title: Lunch
Intelligence Got Cheap. Deciding Didn't

speakers.name: James Bradley
speakers.title: Senior Director, Data Science and Applied AI
speakers.bio: James Bradley is Senior Director of Data Science and Applied AI at Autodesk, leading the machine learning behind how Autodesk goes to market. He is building the decision layer — the personalization, experimentation, and agentic experiences that turn what the company knows into what it does — and champions causal analysis and hypothesis-driven development.

sessions.description: For years the hard question in applied ML was whether a model could do something at all. That constraint is fading. Intelligence is now abundant and composable, so the number of things a system could do has exploded. The scarce capability is deciding well among them. This talk makes the case for the decision layer — the discipline and infrastructure that turn what a company knows into what it does. It closes on Autodesk’s hardest version: a design space that is effectively infinite, where recommendations have to survive physical reality.

sessions.title: Building IAIRO and the need for R&D in India

speakers.name: Amit Sheth
speakers.title: Founding Director
speakers.bio: Amit Sheth is leading the Indian AI Research Organisation's efforts to build sovereign AI systems designed specifically for enterprise and national needs. sessions.description: India’s AI ambitions cannot be realised through adoption alone; they require a strong foundation of homegrown research and innovation. This session will explore the vision behind building the Indian AI Research Organization (IAIRO) and its role in strengthening India’s AI research ecosystem. Amit Sheth will discuss why sustained investment in fundamental and applied R&D is critical for India to develop globally competitive AI capabilities, build indigenous technologies, and address challenges unique to the country. The session will also examine how academia, industry, startups, and government can work together to create an environment that enables long-term AI research and translates breakthroughs into real-world impact.

speakers.name: Ramit Bhardwaj
speakers.title: Chief Technology Officer
speakers.bio: Ramit Bhardwaj, the Chief Technology Officer of IndiQube has been central to driving the evolution of MiQube, IndiQube’s proprietary technology stack that powers its workplace solutions ecosystem. Elaborate Profile : Ramit Rajinder Bhardwaj is the Chief Technology Officer of IndiQube and has been associated with the Company for over six years. He has played a pivotal role in strengthening IndiQube’s technology foundation and in driving the evolution of MiQube, the Company’s proprietary technology stack that powers its workplace solutions ecosystem. sessions.description: The uncomfortable question underneath the GCC boom. India has 1,700+ GCCs and counting. The narrative is that they're moving up the value chain into product, research, and IP. The reality is that many are still cost-arbitrage plays wearing a strategic label.

sessions.title: Lunch
Building Sovereign AI Infrastructure for India

speakers.name: Supriya Paul
speakers.title: Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Supriya Paul is the Co-Founder of Josh Talks and Josh Talks AI. In 2015, she co-founded Josh Talks and built it into one of India's largest vernacular storytelling platforms, with over 40 million subscribers, 3 billion+ lifetime views, and nearly 150 million monthly viewers across Indian languages. That decade-long journey gave her a ground-level understanding of how India actually communicates: across languages, dialects, socioeconomic contexts, and every district of the country. Today, she leads partnerships, ecosystem development, and strategic growth at Josh Talks AI, the company's AI infrastructure division. Josh Talks AI builds research-grade datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation infrastructure that helps the world's frontier AI labs build more reliable voice AI for real-world deployment. Its flagship benchmark, Voice of India built in partnership with AI4Bharat at IIT Madras is India's First Independent Multimodal AI Evaluation Platform Supriya is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader (2026), Forbes 30 Under 30, recipient of the National Media Award from the President of India, and NASSCOM Woman Entrepreneur of the Year. She is a prominent voice on entrepreneurship, women in STEM, human-cantered AI, and building technology for the next billion users.

sessions.description: India’s AI ambition will depend on far more than building powerful models. It will require a robust, trusted and locally relevant AI infrastructure spanning data, compute, evaluation, language capabilities and deployment. As AI becomes increasingly embedded across public services, enterprises and everyday life, building these foundational layers will be critical to ensuring that India is not merely a consumer of global AI, but an active builder of the technology stack. This session will explore what it takes to build sovereign AI infrastructure for a country as diverse and complex as India. From creating high-quality Indic-language datasets and benchmarks to developing systems that can operate across languages, accents, dialects and real-world environments, the discussion will examine the often invisible infrastructure that determines whether AI actually works for India. It will also look at how India can leverage its scale, diversity and unique deployment challenges as a strategic advantage and build AI capabilities that are not only sovereign and trusted, but globally relevant.

sessions.title: Lunch
Future of Content Creation and AI Avatar

speakers.name: Vishal Yoman
speakers.title: Founder & CEO
speakers.bio: Vishal Yoman is the Founder and CEO of Kalpanik Films , a pioneering studio at the forefront of AI-native cinema and generative visual storytelling. Backed by over 14 years of creative direction and filmmaking experience, Vishal bridges classical cinematic language with cutting-edge multi-modal AI pipelines. An alumnus of the Maya Academy of Advanced Creativity and a recipient of the 40 Under 40 distinction at the 24FPS International Animation Awards, he has directed landmark 100% generative AI music videos, high-impact commercial campaigns and original digital IP. A frequent keynote speaker at leading creative and tech forums including Broadcast India and IndiaJoy VFX Summit, Vishal champions directorial control, character consistency and production scalability in the generative media era.

speakers.name: Ayushi Anand
speakers.title: Co-Founder & COO
speakers.bio: Ayushi Anand is the Co-Founder and COO of Kalpanik Films , leading the development of production-grade generative AI workflows, synthetic media architectures, and virtual persona ecosystems. Ayushi specializes in prompt engineering, multi-modal model orchestration, and character consistency across large-scale video pipelines. At Kalpanik Films, she oversees end-to-end studio operations, enterprise client solutions and the technical deployment of synthetic humans for global brand campaigns, microdramas, and entertainment IP. Ayushi is a prominent voice on the commercialization and operational scaling of generative media.We would be excited to share our production-grounded insights and live media case studies on the Cypher stage.

sessions.description: The transition from experimental AI generation to production-scale synthetic media is redefining how creators, brands, and media enterprises produce and distribute content. This session provides an industry-tested exploration into building, scaling, and operationalizing personalized AI avatars and digital humans. Drawing from real-world studio workflows at Kalpanik Films, we will break down the convergence of generative video models, photogrammetry scanning, synthetic voice cloning, and automated pipeline engineering demonstrating how teams can scale digital IP without compromising creative identity, authenticity, or IP governance.

sessions.title: Building next-gen AI & Robotics innovations and innovators for society, economy & sovereignty

speakers.name: Raghu Dharmaraju
speakers.title: CEO
speakers.bio: Raghu Dharmaraju. is a technology, innovation, and social-impact leader with over 25 years of experience building innovation institutions, scaling deep-tech ventures, and translating research into solutions with measurable societal impact. He currently serves as Chief Executive Officer at ARTPARK, where he has helped build a premier AI and robotics innovation ecosystem bringing together startups, industry, academia, government, and the development sector. At ARTPARK, he has helped build and invest in 34 startups, supported and collaborated with 30+ others, and led large-scale AI initiatives across healthcare, climate resilience, agriculture, languages, and public health. He has also contributed to national AI and data initiatives with institutions including IISc, ICMR, NITI Aayog, MeitY, Google, AWS, and the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser. A two-time winner of the Global Grand Challenge for Equitable AI and Grand Challenge India, Raghuram has played a key role in shaping national initiatives around AI for healthcare, physical AI, research translation, pandemic preparedness, and digital public infrastructure. Previously, Raghu was a co-founder and VP – Products & Programs at Wadhwani AI, where he helped establish a globally recognised organisation focused on AI for social good, raising approximately $20 million from organisations including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, USAID, Google.org , and the Botnar Foundation. He has also helped scale award-winning med-tech innovations that reached nearly one million babies across India. Earlier, he led strategy, product management, and startup operations for a global business at Corning Environmental Technologies. His experience spans digital health, med-tech, agriculture, environmental technologies, solar energy, financial inclusion, and the circular economy. An alumnus of IIT Madras, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and Cornell University, Raghuram brings a distinctive perspective at the intersection of deep technology, entrepreneurship, public policy, and inclusive societal impact.

sessions.description: As artificial intelligence and robotics move from experimentation to real-world deployment, the next wave of innovation will be shaped not only by technological breakthroughs, but also by the people, ecosystems, and institutions capable of building and scaling them. This session will explore how India can develop next-generation AI and robotics innovations while nurturing the talent and innovators needed to drive long-term progress. The discussion will examine the convergence of AI, robotics, advanced engineering, and intelligent systems, and how these technologies can create meaningful impact across industries and society. It will also explore the role of research, academia, startups, industry collaboration, and policy in building a robust innovation ecosystem. Beyond commercial applications, the session will look at how indigenous capabilities in AI and robotics can contribute to economic growth, strategic resilience, and technological sovereignty. It will highlight what it takes to move from isolated innovations to scalable solutions—and from individual innovators to a sustained pipeline of talent capable of shaping India's technology future.

sessions.title: Beyond Agents: Building Systems of Enterprise Intelligence

speakers.name: Yeshwant Nayak
speakers.title: Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer
speakers.bio: Yeshwant Nayak is Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer at Relanto, an AI-first technology company combining product innovation with enterprise consulting and engineering. An industry leader and technology entrepreneur with more than two decades of experience, Yeshwant is focused on shaping how enterprises evolve in an AI-native world. His perspective brings together innovation, enterprise intelligence, governance, and the economics of AI to address a larger question: how organizations redesign themselves when intelligence becomes embedded across every function. At Relanto, he is shaping a vision that connects bold ideas with practical enterprise impact and helps define the next generation of intelligent business systems.

speakers.name: TP Vincent
speakers.title: CTO
speakers.bio: Vincent is CTO at Relanto and a technology leader with more than 30 years of experience building intelligent enterprise systems that combine deep domain expertise with software, data, and AI. He specializes in helping organizations operationalize AI by combining enterprise knowledge, business processes, and intelligent agents. His work current focuses on agent observability, validation, governance, and decision intelligence, areas that are becoming critical as enterprises move agentic AI into business-critical operations. Throughout his career, Vincent has partnered with several Fortune 100 technology organizations to build scalable platforms that support planning, decision making, and digital transformation at global scale.

sessions.description: Connecting autonomy, coordination, economics, and business outcomes As enterprises move from isolated agents to increasingly autonomous AI systems, the next challenge is the industrialization of enterprise intelligence . This session explores how organizations can move from individual agent intelligence to coordinated, system-level intelligence across applications, data, workflows, and people. It examines the emerging Coordination Tax created by fragmented agents and competing objectives, the economics of autonomous AI, and the need to measure Intelligence Yield by connecting AI consumption to business outcomes. The next frontier of enterprise AI is not simply deploying more agents, but building systems where intelligence can coordinate, operate, and create measurable value at scale.

sessions.title: From AI Teams to AI Systems: How GCCs Are Rebuilding the Enterprise Workforce

speakers.name: Asha Poulose Johnson
speakers.title: Chief Digital Officer / SVP
speakers.bio: Asha Poulose Johnson is a visionary global technology leader with 25 years of experience across data, analytics, AI, software, and digital transformation in industrial domains including healthcare, energy, and aviation. Asha has held senior leadership roles including CIO and GCC Head, driving large-scale transformation, building high-performing global teams, and creating strategic partnerships that deliver business value. She is also an active industry and board leader, contributing to technology governance, innovation, and diversity initiatives. Passionate about nurturing future talent, she actively engages with early-career professionals and academia.

speakers.name: Vishal Kulshrestha
speakers.title: Head of eCommerce & Omni Channel
speakers.bio: Vishal Kulshrestha is part of the India Site Leadership team at Alshaya Group, with over 28 years of experience across engineering, digital transformation, global delivery and building technology capabilities. His work and thought leadership sit at the intersection of GCC transformation, Enterprise AI, strategy and leadership, with a strong focus on translating technology into practical business outcomes. His current focus includes the practical adoption of AI in large enterprises, from customer experience and engineering productivity to AI governance, operating models and decision-making. He is working across multiple AI initiatives to solve real business problems with clear accountability, measurable outcomes and economic viability. His leadership approach brings together technology, business and people, with a strong belief that sustainable transformation requires more than technology alone. It requires the right capabilities, operating model, leadership and organisational readiness to turn technology into meaningful impact. He is also the author of LeaderSinksShip, a book exploring leadership, people management, organisational behaviour and the principles behind building high-performing teams.

speakers.name: Karan Thapar
speakers.title: Journalist

speakers.name: Shipra Sharma
