speakers.bio: Shipra is a seasoned AI and analytics leader with nearly two decades of experience in building data-driven products and industry solutions. She has led large-scale digital transformation and AI initiatives across global enterprises, having held leadership roles at Bristlecone and Mu Sigma. Her expertise spans AI strategy, data science, and supply chain innovation, with a strong focus on solving complex business challenges through technology. She holds a robust academic foundation in technology and analytics and is recognized for her collaborative leadership and product innovation mindset.

speakers.name: Anees Merchant
speakers.title: Executive Vice President and Business Unit Lead for Technology, Media, Telecom (TMT) & Products and Innovation Lead
speakers.bio: Anees Merchant is Executive Vice President and Business Unit Lead for Technology, Media, Telecom (TMT) & Products and Innovation Lead at C5i. He is responsible for leading the development of intellectual property (IP), frameworks, and solutions leveraging the power of Generative AI and other technologies and providing leadership to Analytics Consulting. Anees is passionate about helping companies grow through a combination of human and machine intelligence and seeks to lead the AI revolution with integrity and impact. Prior to C5i, Anees was an Associate Principal at eClerx Services Ltd. and has worked with companies like Wipro Spectramind Services Pvt. Ltd., Stream Tracmail Pvt. Ltd., Microgate Corporation, IBS Infotech, and Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited. He is a member of the AIM Leaders Council and 3AI Thought Leaders Circle (TLC). sessions.description: GCCs are moving beyond building AI teams to redesigning how work itself gets done. This panel explores how AI is reshaping workforce models, roles, skills, and operating structures within global enterprises and what it takes to build AI-enabled organizations at scale.

sessions.title: Can AI enable Financial Services Distribution to next 300Mn+ customers in Small Towns?

speakers.name: Himanshu Gupta
speakers.title: Co-Founder & Chief AI Officer
speakers.bio: Himanshu Gupta has spent 15+ years building AI systems that make consequential decisions in financial services. At IBM Research and S&P Global, he developed complex predictive AI and machine learning models across industries. At LendingKart, he architected what became one of India's leading AI-driven credit risk engines, building the underwriting infrastructure that allowed the platform to scale lending while keeping defaults in check. He holds a B.Tech from IIT Delhi. At WeRize, he is applying that same rigour to a far harder problem: building an AI system that understands the financial behaviour of small-city India, in its own languages, on its own terms.

sessions.description: Most lending AI in India still operates in English, translated at the edges. WeRize took the opposite bet: build the underwriting agent to think and speak in the customer's own language from the ground up, using lakhs of hours of recorded vernacular customer calls as training data: a data asset competitors can't easily replicate. This talk walks through the architecture of that agent stack: what it takes to run video KYC, bureau pull, and underwriting inside a single voice-first, vernacular conversation; the roadmap toward real-time dynamic pricing based on behavioural and location signals; and the engineering trade-offs of building natively for 8 Indian languages instead of bolting on translation. It also covers an early pilot giving WeRize's 19,000+ freelancer network their own AI-driven digital twins to pre-qualify and sort leads autonomously, a bet on AI making local agents more capable, not redundant.

sessions.title: Kuku’s Storytelling AI Stack Solving for Bharat: AI Built for How Bharat Consumes Content

speakers.name: Lal Chand Bisu
speakers.title: Co-Founder and CEO
speakers.bio: Lal Chand Bisu is the Co-Founder and CEO of Kuku. With over a decade of experience in consumer technology, he has dedicated his career to creating products that expand access to knowledge and opportunity for millions of users in their own languages. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur. After graduation, he chose entrepreneurship and co-founded Edux Solutions Private Limited, an education technology startup and later served as a Team Leader at Topp, where he gained deep expertise in product development and scaling tech-driven education solutions. In 2020, he was featured in the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in the Media, Marketing & Advertising category.

sessions.description: Most AI in content and media was designed to solve a Western problem and then adapted for India. Kuku changed that. Every AI system Kuku has built starts with one question of, “How does Bharat actually discover, consume, and fall in love with a story?” In this session, Lal Chand Bisu, Co-founder and CEO of Kuku will share how the company has built an AI-native entertainment operating mode, where machine learning, generative AI, intelligent agents and Kuku’s data systems power every stage of the storytelling journey. He will cover Kuku’s decision to build its own recommendation engine and how GenAI now runs through the full content production pipeline (ideation, scripting, audio production, video production, promo generation and post-production). The central argument of this session is that the next generation of AI-native companies in India will come from media & entertainment. No other sector is forced to simultaneously solve for language diversity, cultural nuance, low-cost distribution and mass personalisation at scale, in real time. The numbers reflect the scale of this opportunity. The global AI in media and entertainment market, valued at USD 25.98 billion in 2024, is projected to reach USD 99.48 billion by 2030, and India is among its fastest-growing markets, with its AI in M&E segment expected to grow at a CAGR of 30.7% from USD 2.3 billion in 2025 to USD 13.6 billion by 2033. Finally, this session will explore how AI-native storytelling has the potential to reshape the media and entertainment industry from the ground up, and why India, with its population, diversity, its creator ecosystem, and its growing AI-first innovation culture, is uniquely positioned to become the world’s content factory for the AI era. Kuku is building that playbook and the session will give a glimpse of what it looks like from the inside.

sessions.title: Building Voice AI from India, for India, and for the world

speakers.name: Sneha Roy

sessions.description: Voice is emerging as one of the most natural interfaces for AI, and India presents a uniquely complex opportunity with its linguistic diversity, code-switching, varied accents, noisy environments and the need for cost-effective, real-time experiences. speakers.name: Vikas Mathur

sessions.title: AI at Population Scale: Reflections

sessions.title: Conversational AI for the 4 Billion+ non-English global population

speakers.name: Praveen Srivatsa

sessions.title: The Last Human Advantage: Leadership Presence in the Age of AI

This is more than a talk about human skills. Through a brief live experience, you’ll feel the difference presence makes and leave with something you can use in your next important conversation.

Drawing from real-world experience in supply chain, manufacturing, and digital transformation, the session will also explore what it takes to scale AI beyond pilots—from building the right data and technology foundations to redesigning processes, empowering teams, and aligning AI initiatives with measurable business value.

sessions.title: Role of quantum technologies in AI and vice versa

speakers.name: Arindam Ghosh
speakers.title: Professor

His research focuses on electronic transport in two-dimensional systems, graphene and other atomically thin materials, quantum dots and wires, single-electron transport, and charge and spin effects at the nanoscale. Prof. Ghosh has built an extensive academic and research career at IISc, following his PhD in Physics from the institute and postdoctoral research at the Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge. He has received several prestigious recognitions, including the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology and the Infosys Prize in Physical Sciences, for his contributions to experimental condensed matter physics and the development of emerging two-dimensional materials and devices. He is also closely involved in India's quantum technology ecosystem and has contributed to the vision for the National Quantum Mission.

sessions.description: Artificial intelligence and quantum technologies are two of the most important components in today’s technology landscape. While quantum technologies can add several dimensions to the emerging landscape in AI, for example, by reducing the energy overhead in computational demands or exponential speed-ups in certain applications, AI can also make several contributions in the development and field deployment of the quantum technologies. In this session I shall focus on the quantum technologies, explain the basic concepts and outline some of its symbiotic engagements with AI.

sessions.title: What Comes After Generative AI? AI That Can Design the Physical World

speakers.name: Arastu Sharma
speakers.title: CEO
speakers.bio: Dr. Arastu is a technology leader, AI researcher, and entrepreneur working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, advanced research, and education. He currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of Shodh AI and Aestr by GyanVihar , where he is focused on building and advancing AI-led solutions and initiatives. He is also a Board Member at Suresh Gyan Vihar University , contributing to the institution’s broader vision around technology, innovation, and the future of education. Alongside his entrepreneurial and leadership roles, Dr. Arastu has been associated with the University of Cambridge as a Microsoft Researcher since 2019 , bringing a strong research-oriented perspective to his work in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. With a career spanning AI research, technology, entrepreneurship, and academia , Dr. Arastu brings a multidisciplinary perspective to the rapidly evolving AI landscape. His work reflects a focus on translating cutting-edge research into practical applications while exploring how AI can drive innovation across industries and create meaningful impact at scale. Through his leadership and research, Dr. Arastu continues to contribute to conversations around the future of AI, technological innovation, and the role of research-driven approaches in building the next generation of intelligent systems.

sessions.description: Generative AI has transformed our ability to create text, images and software. But what happens when we ask AI not just to generate information, but to design something that must actually work in the physical world? Imagine asking for a better battery, a higher-yield bioprocess, a new material or a more efficient manufacturing process — and having an AI system reason backwards from the desired outcome to the molecules, conditions and processes needed to create it. This talk explores the evolution from generative AI toward Physical AI and scientific foundation models, the challenges of reasoning across the different scales of the physical world, and how work being built in India today could contribute to the next major generation of global AI systems.

sessions.description: What can AI really understand from a satellite image? In this hands-on workshop, participants will explore how satellite imagery can be transformed into intelligence using modern AI and geospatial techniques. The session will take participants through a practical workflow—from working with satellite imagery to extracting spectral information, combining geospatial datasets, and applying machine learning and deep learning for image understanding. Participants will work with real-world Earth observation data from NASA and explore techniques such as image classification, segmentation, change detection and transfer learning. The workshop will demonstrate how these approaches can support real-world applications including agricultural monitoring, land-use mapping, infrastructure and urban monitoring, disaster response etc. The session will also introduce the emerging role of geospatial foundation models and GeoAI, showing how pretrained representations can be adapted to specialised Earth observation tasks. Designed as an interactive, learn-by-doing session, the workshop will take participants on a journey from satellite pixels to AI-powered Earth intelligence, giving them practical exposure to interesting business use cases across all industries.

sessions.title: India’s AI Advantage: We Have More Than Data

sessions.description: India’s AI opportunity goes beyond the sheer volume of data available to its enterprises and consumers. The challenge is to translate these inherent advantages into meaningful AI innovation that is both globally competitive and relevant to India’s needs. The session will examine how product innovation, talent, accessibility, contextual intelligence, and India’s ability to operate at population scale can shape a distinctive AI advantage, enabling solutions that are built in India and have the potential to serve the world.

sessions.title: Token Tax Saver Schemes: 7 Design Choice Hacks

speakers.name: Moumita Sarker
speakers.title: Founder and CEO
speakers.bio: Moumita Sarker is the Founder and CEO of Illuminati Consulting, an AI consulting firm that helps businesses unlock measurable value through practical, purpose-driven AI solutions. With over 21 years of experience, she has witnessed every major evolution in AI and analytics, from traditional statistical modelling and machine learning to today's Agentic AI, giving her a pragmatic, business-first perspective on technology adoption and value realization. She has led transformative AI and analytics programs across banking, retail, QSR, hospitality, insurance, automotive, construction, and CPG, delivering solutions in sales acceleration, customer lifecycle management, end-to-end agentic transformation, dynamic pricing and promotions, predictive maintenance, forecasting, and AI for CFOs. Prior to founding Illuminati Consulting, she headed the Agentic AI Centre of Excellence for Deloitte South Asia and was a founding member of Cartesian Consulting. Her earlier experience includes J.P. Morgan and HDFC Bank, where she began her analytics journey. An alumna of the Indian Statistical Institute, Moumita combines deep expertise in Agentic AI, Generative AI, Machine Learning, business analytics, and statistical modelling with a strong focus on commercially viable outcomes. sessions.description: Wondering why financial planning is referenced in this topic? Imagine you want to achieve a crucial goal for your required retirement fund, and you keep optimising your money allocation vehicles along the way; you'd lose opportunities through experimentation. Rather, we all build our own financial planning playbook. Extending that thought, why do we have to pay that extra token tax to achieve core business agentic goals when you can design a process playbook with planned choices and levers before you start optimising token economics in production? Token efficiency starts with design. Design choices and some known technology levers can help achieve the balancing act between token consumption, latency, and performance. This session explores 7 Design Hacks to build AI systems with better economics —from architecture implants, model selection, ML-coexistent approaches, human-agent co-delivery, and smart controls—tested in production and proven to work. The focus is on better economics without compromising on outcomes —achieving the same or better business outcomes through smarter AI design. Won't just explain the hacks; will demonstrate them in the session.

sessions.description: Practical lessons from integrating third-party AI into banking operations while balancing innovation with regulatory obligations.

sessions.title: Building Meaning-First AI in India: The Sphota Architecture

speakers.name: Siddharth Panwar
speakers.title: Chief Executive Officer | Professor
speakers.bio: Dr. Siddharth Panwar is an Assistant Professor at IIT Mandi and the Chief Executive Officer of NeuroDx, where he is working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, neuroscience, signal processing, and diagnostic medicine. He holds a PhD from IIT Delhi and master’s and undergraduate degrees in Electrical Engineering from Stanford University and the University of Arizona, respectively. His research focuses on NeuroAI, neural signal processing, machine learning, and foundation models for EEG and other physiological signals. At NeuroDx, he is leading the development of AI systems designed to advance brain health, neurological diagnostics, and next-generation neurotechnology. His work bridges academic research and real-world healthcare applications, with a focus on building clinically meaningful AI that can improve accessibility and precision in neurological care.

sessions.description: Most contemporary artificial intelligence systems operate within the same broad paradigm: intelligence is only learned through the prediction and generation of language tokens, with capability increasing primarily through scale. These systems have achieved extraordinary results, but they leave open a fundamental question: must language also be the computational substrate of intelligence, or can models reason over representations of meaning more directly? This talk introduces Sphota, a brain-inspired, semantic-first architecture being developed in India. Sphota separates the formation of an active meaning representation from lexical memory and language generation. Computation operates over this evolving semantic representation, while language remains the interface through which knowledge is received and expressed. The talk will explain the architectural principles behind Sphota and present empirical results from compact models across multiple scales, including comparisons of task performance, memory requirements and computational efficiency with established language models. It will also distinguish the capabilities demonstrated by current models from the larger architectural hypotheses still being investigated. The broader argument is that “Make AI in India” should mean more than training existing architectures on Indian infrastructure and data. India must also develop original architectures shaped by its scientific capabilities, computational constraints and deployment needs.

With a strong background in tech leadership and AI strategy, Aaditya helps organizations unlock the full potential of their data and AI initiatives, enabling them to modernize capabilities, drive innovation, and achieve sustainable impact. Known for his ability to bridge technical excellence with strategic vision, he works closely with cross-functional teams to design and implement AI frameworks that align with long-term business objectives. Aaditya’s expertise spans AI adoption, data strategy, and technology transformation, making him a trusted partner for businesses looking to thrive in an increasingly digital and data-centric world.

sessions.description: The debate the sovereign AI conversation avoids. Twelve foundation models, 100,000 GPUs, $200B investment target — but Sarvam 105B is still not competing with GPT-5 or Claude at the frontier. Is the gap closing or widening? One side argues that India's frugal-innovation model plus data advantages will eventually produce a genuine frontier player. The other argues that compute economics and talent flow to the US make this structurally impossible until 2030+. This is the debate the ecosystem has in private and never on stage.

sessions.title: The Pursuit of Voice AI for All - Beyond urban boundaries

speakers.name: Prasanta Kumar Ghosh
speakers.title: Professor
speakers.bio: Prasanta Kumar Ghosh is a Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. He holds a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Southern California and has previously worked with IBM India Research Lab and Microsoft Research India. At IISc, he leads research in speech and audio processing, with a focus on non-linear signal processing, speech production and perception, and automatic speech recognition. His work explores the intersection of speech science, signal processing, and AI, with a strong emphasis on developing speech technologies inspired by the way humans produce and perceive sound. With an academic and research career spanning advanced speech technologies and signal processing, Prof. Ghosh has received several recognitions for his research and teaching, including the INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship from the Department of Science and Technology, the best M.Sc . (Engineering) thesis award at IISc, and awards for excellence in teaching at USC. He currently leads the Speech Processing, Information, Reasoning and Engineering (SPIRE) Lab at IISc, where his work contributes to advancing research in speech, audio, and intelligent systems.

sessions.description: Voice AI has the potential to become one of the most inclusive interfaces for India’s next billion users, particularly those beyond urban and English-first ecosystems. This session will explore how advances in speech recognition, multilingual AI, and conversational technologies can bring AI to people in their own languages, accents, and local contexts. From rural communities and agriculture to healthcare, education, and public services, the discussion will examine what it takes to build Voice AI that works reliably beyond cities—not just by translating languages, but by understanding the diversity of India’s voices. It will also explore the technology, data, ecosystem, and trust challenges that must be addressed to make truly accessible Voice AI a reality for all.

sessions.title: The Nervous System of Bharat - Building a Agent Network That Senses, Predicts, and Heals Itself

speakers.name: Shalabh Aggarwal
speakers.title: CTO
speakers.bio: Shalabh Aggarwal is a strategic technology leader and currently serves as Chief Technology Officer at Spice Money. With 15+ years of experience across FinTech, B2B SaaS, and enterprise technology, he specializes in building and scaling AI-driven platforms, leading 0→1 and 1→10 product journeys, and aligning technology strategy with business outcomes. Previously, as CTO at Credflow and VP Engineering at SAVii, Shalabh led digital lending transformations, built AI-powered financial products, and modernized technology infrastructure to drive scalability and efficiency. At Credflow, he spearheaded the development of a modular digital lending stack, re-architected legacy systems, and optimized cloud infrastructure to significantly reduce costs while supporting rapid scale. An engineer at heart, Shalabh brings deep expertise in AI, cloud infrastructure, modern system architectures, and product engineering. He is also the author of the Flask Framework Cookbook series and an early open-source contributor, combining strong technical depth with a product-focused approach to technology leadership.

speakers.name: Hardeep Sharma
speakers.title: Deputy CTO
speakers.bio: Hardeep Sharma is an engineering leader and Deputy Chief Technology Officer & Head of UX at Spice Money, with 12+ years of experience building and scaling high-impact fintech platforms used by millions of users. His expertise spans system architecture, platform engineering, fraud and risk systems, AI-driven automation, distributed systems, and product strategy. At Spice Money, Hardeep has held progressively senior leadership roles across engineering, digital products, mobility, data, and design thinking. In his current role, he focuses on driving technology strategy, building scalable and reliable platforms, strengthening transaction integrity, and leveraging AI and intelligent automation to solve complex business challenges. With an engineering-first approach complemented by product depth and design thinking, Hardeep is passionate about building high-performance engineering cultures and simplifying complex technology to create meaningful solutions for real-world users.

sessions.description: Somewhere in rural India, right now, a network of over a million human nodes is generating one of the richest, least-observed signals in the country - the real pulse of the Bharat economy, one AEPS withdrawal, one wallet top-up, one shop visit at a time. Almost all of that signal vanishes the instant it's created. This talk is about what happens when it doesn't. I'll walk through how we're building Network Intelligence at Spice Money - a system designed to sense the live state of a million-agent financial network, predict what's about to happen to it, act through the humans already embedded inside it, and learn from whether that action actually worked. A distributor running dry the morning subsidies land. An agent quietly drifting to a competitor weeks before the transaction numbers would ever show it. A rupee of retention spend that either earns its keep against a measured control group or gets pulled. Underneath all of it, the rarer case - a fraud ring hiding in the shape of a graph, invisible to any rule that looks at one transaction at a time.

sessions.title: The Trust Deficit: Building Responsible AI in a Regulated, Risk-Heavy Business

speakers.name: Ramesh Aithal
speakers.title: Chief Digital Officer
speakers.bio: Ramesh Aithal is the Chief Digital Officer at L&T Finance, where he leads the company's digital transformation, AI, and technology strategy. With over 25 years of experience, he has held leadership roles at Elastic, Zenefits, Goldman Sachs, Ness Technologies, and Citibank, driving large-scale engineering, cloud, and digital innovation initiatives. Passionate about building AI-powered, customer-centric financial services, Ramesh brings deep expertise in enterprise technology, digital lending, and intelligent automation.

sessions.description: As AI becomes increasingly embedded in financial services, the challenge is no longer simply about adopting the technology—it is about earning and sustaining trust. In a highly regulated and risk-sensitive industry, AI decisions can directly influence customers, credit outcomes, fraud detection, compliance, and business operations, making transparency, accountability, and governance critical. This session will explore how financial institutions can build responsible AI frameworks that balance innovation with risk management and regulatory expectations. It will examine the importance of explainability, data governance, model oversight, bias mitigation, and human accountability in deploying AI at scale. The discussion will also look at how organizations can move beyond compliance-led approaches to create AI systems that are trustworthy by design, enabling innovation while protecting customers and strengthening institutional confidence.

sessions.title: From Bangalore to the World: Building Global AI Solutions with Indian Innovation

speakers.title: Corporate Vice President & Managing Director
speakers.bio: Mohan Rao Goli is a distinguished technology leader and one of the prominent voices shaping the future of global innovation and emerging technologies. With over 29 years of industry experience, he currently serves as Corporate Vice President and Managing Director of Samsung Electronics’s Samsung R&D Institute India – Bangalore (SRI-B) — one of Samsung’s largest and most strategic R&D centres worldwide. In this role, Mohan leads large-scale engineering and research initiatives that power Samsung’s next generation of intelligent products and services. Under his leadership, SRI-B plays a pivotal role in advancing Samsung’s global technology roadmap across multiple business verticals, driving innovation in artificial intelligence, advanced communications, and next-generation consumer technologies. Prior to assuming his current role, Mohan served as the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of SRI-B, where he was responsible for defining the institute’s technical vision and strengthening its core engineering capabilities. During his tenure as CTO, he spearheaded the transformation of SRI-B into a leading AI Excellence Hub, enabling the development of cutting-edge technologies while nurturing world-class engineering talent. His leadership contributed significantly to the development of several breakthrough AI initiatives, including Galaxy AI, a suite of advanced on-device and cloud-based artificial intelligence capabilities designed to redefine the mobile experience. Mohan also brings deep technical expertise in advanced communication research and development, with extensive experience across 5G and 6G standards, next-generation wireless systems, and the development and deployment of 5G terminal and network solutions within the global ecosystem. A prolific innovator, he holds over 70 patents globally, spanning communication networks, next-generation wireless technologies, and AI-driven communication systems. His current areas of interest include AI/ML-driven wireless technologies, next-generation communication systems, and Extended Reality (XR). Throughout his distinguished career, Mohan has received several prestigious recognitions for his leadership and contributions to technological innovation. These include Zinnov’s “High Impact Global Role” Award (2019) and “Best in Class CoE” Award (2022), along with the “Best Overseas R&D Employee” Award presented twice by the President of Samsung Electronics. In 2024, he was honored as “CTO of the Year” by the Indian Achievers’ Forum and recognized as the “Zinnov Tech Role Model 2024.” Beyond his professional achievements, Mohan is deeply committed to nurturing future talent and strengthening India’s technology ecosystem. He actively champions Samsung’s flagship CSR initiatives such as Samsung Innovation Campus, which equips young Indians with future-ready technology skills, and Solve for Tomorrow, a national innovation program that empowers youth to develop solutions for real-world challenges. sessions.description: India’s AI journey is evolving from being a hub for technology talent to becoming a global centre for AI innovation. This session explores how Indian R&D teams are moving beyond execution to conceptualising, building, and scaling AI solutions that address complex global challenges. Drawing on Samsung’s innovation ecosystem in India, the session will examine how world-class talent, deep engineering capabilities, and a strong culture of innovation can help build AI products and solutions from Bangalore for markets around the world. It will also explore the role of AI research, responsible innovation, and collaboration between industry and academia in shaping globally competitive technologies. The discussion will highlight what it takes to transform India’s engineering strength into enduring AI leadership and how solutions built in India can create impact far beyond its borders.

sessions.title: AI Reads the Manual. Your Company Never Wrote One.

speakers.name: Sravanth Aluru
speakers.title: CEO and Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Sravanth Aluru is the CEO of Avataar.ai , which he co-founded over a decade ago as an AI- transformation partner for large global enterprises. Avataar works across industries including Real Estate, Healthcare, Retail, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain, building agentic, self-learning AI platforms that operate real-world workflows at scale and deliver durable enterprise impact. An engineer from IIT Bombay, Sravanth began his career in the early 2000s at Microsoft, at a time when AI was still commonly discussed in terms of “fuzzy” systems. He witnessed first-hand the evolution of intelligent systems—from early fuzzy and neuro-fuzzy approaches to the neural architectures that define modern AI today. These formative years shaped his conviction that intelligence would ultimately live at the core of platforms and organizations, not as surface-level features or tools. After earning his MBA from The Wharton School, Sravanth spent the early 2010s on Wall Street, advising technology founders and boards on global scale-ups, M&A, and public listings. From that vantage point, he observed a decisive shift: the world’s leading technology companies began redirecting both organic investment and acquisitions toward foundational AI platforms—laying the groundwork for the AI transformation now unfolding across every major industry. Today, Sravanth’s focus is on building Central Organizational Brains—domain-specific, agentic intelligence layers that move far beyond copilots and pilots. These systems embed intelligence directly into how organizations operate, learn, and make decisions, enabling compounding productivity gains, durable value creation, and defensible competitive moats over time. In parallel, Avataar is an active partner in the IndiaAI Mission, contributing to the design of UAI (Universal AI Infrastructure)—often described as a “UPI for AI”—a foundational, interoperable layer for deploying and scaling domain-specific AI across sectors. Avataar has raised over $55M, backed by Sequoia Capital and Tiger Global, and operates out of San Francisco and Bangalore. Sravanth is a lead inventor on 10+ U.S. patents across AI and computer vision and works closely with enterprises, governments, and ecosystem partners to shape the next phase of AI-native organizations.

sessions.description: Almost every large company now uses AI. Almost none of them can find it in their profits. Eighty per cent of executives say AI has made them personally more productive. Six per cent of organisations can attribute more than five per cent of earnings to it - and that six per cent has not moved in a year. The technology works. It is not reaching the P&L. This session treats that as a plumbing problem and follows the money. It opens by correcting the most-quoted statistic in enterprise AI - the claim that 95% of AI pilots fail, which does not survive contact with its own source - and then traces five specific places where the value leaks out between the desk and the balance sheet. The largest leak is that almost nothing a company really knows has ever been written down. The real process is not in the manual; it lives in the exceptions, the workarounds and the judgment of people who have been there fifteen years. AI can only work with what it can read. Sravanth calls this the representation gap, and it is the single biggest reason AI projects stall after a promising pilot. He sets out five practical moves that close each leak in turn — including why agents cannot safely be trusted to act until the business has been written down, and why the corrections your people make are both the training data that makes AI cheaper and the asset most enterprises are currently giving away for nothing. With a live demonstration, and two questions every executive should put to any AI vendor, including this one.

sessions.title: The Scaling Loop: The Secret Relationship Between Small and Big Models

speakers.name: Ganesh Ramakrishnan
speakers.title: Founding Director | Professor,
speakers.bio: Ganesh Ramakrishnan is Founding Director of BharatGen, India's first government-backed, open-source, multilingual foundation model initiative launched in October 2024, spanning text, speech, and document vision models across 22+ Indic languages. His research in natural language processing, generative AI, and human-assisted machine learning defines BharatGen's approach: building large language models on small, carefully curated datasets to make high-quality AI viable in low-resource settings. After earning his PhD from IIT Bombay in 2004, he joined IBM Research India, working on scalable information extraction, before returning as faculty in 2009. He led research in statistical relational learning and machine translation, producing Udaan, an end-to-end machine translation ecosystem for Indian languages, and DECILE, a data-efficient machine learning framework for resource-constrained environments. He has collaborated extensively with IBM Research, Adobe, and Google, and his work has appeared in AAAI, ACL, NeurIPS, ICML, and EMNLP; he serves as area chair for AAAI and ACL. Beyond research, he is Institute Chair Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, holds the Bank of Baroda Chair Professorship in Digital Entrepreneurship, and heads the Koita Centre for Digital Health at IIT Bombay. He has been globally recognised as one of the five Goalkeeper Champions by the Gates Foundation (2026), and featured among AIM 100 Most Influential Global AI Leaders (2026 and 2024), MIT Sloan India's AI50 (2026), and Forbes India's Top 30 AI Minds (2025). He is also a recipient of the Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam HPC & AI Award (2026) and the National Gold Award for eGovernance (2022).

sessions.description: At MLDS 2026, Prof. Ganesh Ramakrishnan introduced frugally scalable AI. This session picks up that thread and asks the harder question underneath it: why does constraint produce better models? BharatGen has built text foundational models across 22 scheduled Indian languages at four different scales, under real resource limits, and learned something at each one that changed the next. This session is about what that sequence taught us, and why the choice between building small and building large turns out not to be a choice at all.

sessions.title: Building Frontier, Sovereign AI from India

speakers.name: Ganesh Gopalan
speakers.title: CEO & Co-Founder
speakers.bio: Ganesh Gopalan is the CEO and Co-Founder of gnani.ai , a frontier Voice AI company backed by Samsung Ventures and InfoEdge. With a deep-tech background at Texas Instruments, Ganesh has built his career at the intersection of semiconductor technology, AI, and enterprise innovation. At gnani.ai , he leads corporate strategy and execution, with a strong focus on building and owning the core technology stack required for agentic AI. Under his leadership, the company has developed inya.ai , a voice-first agentic AI platform featuring advanced ASR, human-like TTS and voice cloning, and industry-specific small language models. The platform operates at significant scale, handling over 4 million daily voice AI agent interactions and approximately 40,000 concurrent voice AI requests. Ganesh is particularly focused on the evolution from Generative AI to Agentic Workforce Automation, where AI agents move beyond answering queries to autonomously driving outcomes and transforming human-machine communication.

sessions.description: As AI becomes increasingly central to enterprise and national competitiveness, the ability to build and control foundational AI capabilities is becoming a strategic imperative. India has the talent, data diversity and growing compute infrastructure to move beyond being a consumer of global AI models and become a builder of frontier technology. This session explores what it takes to build frontier, sovereign AI from India—from foundational models and compute infrastructure to multilingual data, talent and real-world deployment. Drawing from the experience of building AI systems for Indian languages and enterprise environments, the discussion will examine how homegrown models can deliver greater control, privacy, contextual relevance and cost efficiency while addressing India’s unique requirements. The session will also look at the IndiaAI Mission and the emerging ecosystem of Indian AI companies building open and sovereign models, and what it will take for India to develop globally competitive AI capabilities that can serve both Indian enterprises and international markets.

speakers.name: Arjun Erigaisi
speakers.title: Indian chess grandmaster
speakers.bio: Arjun Kumar Erigaisi (born 3 September 2003) [2] is an Indian chess grandmaster . A chess prodigy , he earned the title of grandmaster at the age of 14 years, 11 months, 13 days. In September 2024, he became India's top rated player, and in December 2024, he achieved his peak rating of 2801, making him the fifteenth-highest rated player in history and second Indian ever to cross the 2800 threshold after Viswanathan Anand . [3] Arjun won the double bronze medal at the FIDE World Rapid & Blitz Championships 2025, becoming the first Indian player to register podium finishes at both events since Viswanathan Anand won the Rapid section and finished third in Blitz in 2017. [4] He has sometimes been described as a 'madman' over the board for his bold and unpredictable style. [5]

speakers.bio: Over 15 years, Lokesh has led GCCs, startups, and MNCs in the corporate world with his passionate intrapreneurial style. But there is a Chess side to his story. Chess has been constant in his life since age 6, but now he has been playing multiple roles in elite chess events across the globe. He is associated with various chess tournaments, including the Global Chess League, Norway Chess, World Rapid Blitz, World Cup, and World Championship! His own channel has over 200K+ followers with average monthly viewership 10M+. His goal is to take chess to every individual on the planet by making it more relatable & position it as a life skill! AIM Chess League helps in that way, taking chess to top tech minds across India via online competitions & over the board city events! Technology & Chess have a high correlation in terms of competence & way of doing it better! I look forward to connecting with you all at CYPHER'26 over 3 days in Bengaluru!

sessions.description: What does it take to win at the highest level when technology can calculate millions of moves in seconds? In this fireside chat, Grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi explores the mindset behind his rise to India’s No. 1 across three formats, his fearless creativity famously described as the “Madman” by Magnus Carlsen and the role of AI and engines in modern chess. From beating Magnus to the evolving role of coaches, the rise of younger players and the power of partnerships with brands like Quantbox and BMW, Arjun shares lessons on creativity, decision-making and staying ahead in an AI-powered world. A candid conversation on what chess can teach technology leaders about thinking differently, taking risks and making the next move.

sessions.description: Distinguish which stages of an AI pipeline are genuinely SLM-appropriate (classification, extraction, routing, reranking) vs. which still need an LLM (open-ended synthesis, ambiguity resolution, judgment calls) Design and assemble a hybrid SLM/LLM pipeline with explicit per-stage model selection, rather than defaulting to "call the biggest model for everything." Extend a passive RAG pipeline into an agentic one — query rewriting, self-reflection, multi-agent routing — and measure whether the added reasoning is actually worth it Evaluate a hybrid system with real metrics: quality, latency (P50/P95), cost per query, and the SLM-vs-LLM call mix — not just whether it produced a plausible-looking answer.
